title.narrative: Togo Public Sector Strengthening for Service Delivery Operation

description.narrative: The PforR development objective is to enhance human resource and public expenditure management.

The proposed Investment Project Financing (IPF) component will support the PforR operation, which is the first of its kind in Togo. As such, it is necessary to support the Government with complementary Technical Assistance (TA) in the form of an IPF component that will continue to strengthen the Government's capacity and provide specialized support and high-level technical expertise for the implementation of the Program's results areas: (i) strengthening of the public administration and (ii) improving Public Expenditure Management Efficiency. The TA component will include analytical and advisory services. It will also finance the contracting of a Third-Party Verification Agency and assist the Cour des Comptes (Supreme Audit institution) in creating the capacity to lead the verification of subsequent Programs for Results (PforRs) and the periodic Financial Audit of the IPF component.Specific assistance, in the form of specialized and high-level technical expertise, will mainly focus on providing: (i) high-level advisory support on the drafting of the new civil service law and implementation of the legal framework; (ii) change management and communications strategies on civil service reform; (iii) studies to support the restructuring and institutional re-organization at ministries levels; (iv) diagnostics and preparation for the implementation the biometric census; (v) quality GovTech solutions (e-payment, e-procurement); (vi); seminars and capacity-building on how to conduct negotiations with ICT providers, mobile operators; (vii) development and implementation support of the blueprint of the education sector ICT strategy and the health sector ICT strategy (Schema Directeur); (viii) knowledge exchange activities; (ix) third Party Verification Agency combined with TA to the Cour des Comptes on Verification of the PforR; (x) Financial Audit of IPF component; (xi) support to set up the PforR M&E system to track implementation progress and coordination; (xii) support to establish an ICT-based Grievance Redress Mechanism and beneficiary satisfaction; (xiii) development of an integrated Management information system and dashboards (Prime minister's office; CPES); (xiv) development of Government strategies and policies; (xv) PFM good practices, manual, and dissemination; and (xiii) e-procurement preparation activities. The Ministry of Civil Service will implement the TA in Lome, the capital city. The IPF component is not expected to have any activities that require public works, which may require land acquisition or economic and physical displacement.The Country Partnership Framework (CPF) for FY17-20, extended to the end of FY22 to strengthen core institutions for service delivery, is the first World Bank Group (WBG) country strategy since 1995, and the new CPF that is in preparation. The PforR is aligned with the CPF, as well as the Africa West Region (AFW) Governance Priority, which addresses the International Development Association (IDA) priorities of jobs and economic transformation and the IDA special theme of Fragility, Conflict, and Violence (FCV). Critical to this theme is building the state's legitimacy and capacity, inclusive institutions, and renewing the social contract between citizens and the state towards achieving Universal Health Coverage (UHC). The current proposed program falls directly within the scope of the CPF's Foundational and Cross Cutting Theme: Strengthen Governance and Consolidate Peace, as it will address challenges mentioned in the CPF of poor governance (weak government effectiveness, control of corruption, and accountability) and will seek to improved value for money in public expenditures, strengthened institutions and increased citizen engagement.
